blueprint_tool_entry: The Graph as PASS.md B2 defines it: typed nodes, typed edges (existence / interface / implementation) - F-b2-04. No adapter row exists for the Graph itself in PASS.md Part A; core-graph-implement's own open_questions section recommends, and this harness follows, adapting the record store node and edge assertions round-trip through instead - the JSONL, hash-chained ledger F-b3-17 names, kb/ledger.jsonl and tools/kb.py, the same live instance harness/state-persistence adapts.
standard: none to adopt; typed nodes and three typed edge kinds per PASS.md B2 (F-b2-04)

measured.dryrun: bash harness/core-graph/test.sh on 2026-09-03: passed 20, failed 0. conformance PASSED 10/10 against the in-memory dry-run adapter: every closed node kind admitted and 'widget' refused graph-assertion-invalid 422; one edge of each of the three edge kinds (implementation, existence, interface) admitted; an implementation edge into a document node refused; an existence edge between two implementation nodes refused (design rule 1); a malformed edge (an extra field) refused before it was applied; neighbors found exactly the one implementation reachable in one hop for an interface; path_exists found a path within max_depth=5 and refused it within max_depth=1; retract left the edge absent from the fold but the original record on file; validate ran over a graph value with no store attached; the 300-edge property test (seed=1) found 176 rejections and 0 false_accepts against an independently authored oracle. The minimal call is 27 lines of caller code (under 40) and names no adapter storage file; call.py's table reported the ill-typed edge refused as urn:agentic:problem:graph-assertion-invalid, 1 implementer found, the edge retracted, and both stores agreeing; DRYRUN_FAIL=1 exits 2 typed adapter-unavailable.
measured.swap: conformance PASSED 10/10 before (dryrun, single mutable list, order is append order) and 10/10 after (second, self-identified records under a directory, position claimed by cursor compare-and-swap) with the same 10 cases; sha256 of interface.py+call.py+conformance.py identical across both runs, so the swap was configuration; 4 execution-model axes differ (execution_model text, adapter entity, observed marker dryrun-graph-store vs eventlog-cursor-cas, declared_gaps 0 vs 1); the same caller code (call.py) ran unchanged on both. Cross-store check (core-graph-implement's own definition of done): the identical 5-record assertion log (3 nodes, 2 edges, one retracted) folded and validated on dryrun and second produced identical reports - nodes_checked=3, edges_checked=1, rejections=0, false_accepts=0 on both - verdict_mismatches=0. The live adapter's read path (graph_value via _read_all) was separately exercised read-only against a scratch copy of this repository's real kb/ledger.jsonl (126 real lines preserved, plus 3 fabricated graph_partition-tagged records appended): the fold recovered exactly the 2 nodes and 1 edge appended, and validate reported rejections=0, false_accepts=0; no write was ever sent to the real file.
measured.breakage: interface.check_edge_type was monkeypatched in-process to accept any node kind as an implementation edge's target - the exact widening core-graph's definition of done names - changing nothing else. Under the widened checker, an implementation edge from an implementation node to a document node was wrongly admitted (found on the very first case, well under the DoD's 'in under 100 generated cases' bound) and the widened checker itself reported rejections=0 for it. conformance.py's _oracle_invalid - a ground-truth rule written independently of interface.check_edge_type, imported fresh and never patched - still correctly marked that edge invalid, so the run reported false_accepts=1 via the oracle while the widened checker's own rejections stayed at 0: the report names which rule was widened rather than only that something failed.

claimed: live mode until run on the host: adapters/live.py's write path (subprocess tools/kb.py ledger) has never been invoked from this harness, since appending unreviewed test records into the project's actual kb/ledger.jsonl was judged out of scope for a dry run; only its read path was measured, against a scratch copy

the second adapter's real served-log transport: GRAPH_EVENTLOG_DIR was exercised only against a local scratch directory under harness/core-graph/out; a networked event log with an external cursor consumer has never been pointed at, though the self-identified-record and cursor-CAS design is written to need nothing more from a real one

concurrent writers racing the second adapter's cursor claim is claimed by design (the rename is atomic, the sequence is re-read on every claim), not exercised: this harness's conformance run is single-process and sequential

the pending problem-registry row: urn:agentic:problem:graph-assertion-invalid is this harness's own name, following core-graph's stated default (reuse document-invalid or mint a registered row); docs/decomposition.md section 2.1.6 has no row for a refused graph assertion yet, so this type is proposed, not registered

the two open questions core-graph itself leaves open - whether an agent is its own node kind, and whether one existence edge type is enough for both containment and derivation - are not resolved by this harness; it ships the five node kinds and three edge types as specified

the full 10,000-graph, seeded property-test tool named in core-graph's own definition of done (tools/graph_typecheck.py) was not built as a standalone CLI; this harness's conformance.py exercises the same shape (a generated corpus, an independent oracle, rejections>0, false_accepts==0) at a smaller scale (300 edges) inside the harness's own gate
